findings.cross_file_justification: The test pins the behaviour of tools/ceiling-probe-live.py: when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is unset the probe resolves `claude` from PATH and the calibration record stores `cli_bin == "claude"` (bare name) rather than the resolved absolute path. The record feeds `--write-catalog` into .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml with `source: operator_set, method: probed_headless`.
findings.description: The calibration record that becomes catalog provenance records the CLI as the bare PATH name `claude`, not the resolved absolute path (and no digest). The first test shows the record does carry a full path when CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is set, so provenance quality depends on how the operator invoked the tool. A catalog entry written from a PATH-shadowed or wrapper `claude` is indistinguishable from one written from the real CLI.
findings.failure_mode: An operator or CI job with a shadowed `claude` earlier on PATH (wrapper script, stale install, planted binary) produces a `clean` record that writes a bogus `effective_input_ceiling` into the shared defaults catalog, and the record offers no way to tell which binary produced it.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the probe resolve the binary with shutil.which() before the --version call, record the absolute path (and optionally a sha256 of the file) in `cli_bin`, and refuse to `--write-catalog` when resolution fails. Update the test to assert the resolved path, e.g. `record["cli_bin"] == str(bindir / "claude")`.

findings.trigger_anchor: env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "PYTHONPATH")}
findings.description: The out-of-process test forwards the developer's entire environment to the child except two deny-listed names. Other credential-bearing variables that the real Claude CLI honours (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN for Bedrock) still reach the subprocess. Exposure is currently nil because CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN is pinned to the recording fake and PATH is emptied, so the deny-list is doing no real work and gives a false sense that credentials were scrubbed.
findings.failure_mode: If a future edit loosens the binary pin (for example to test PATH fallback out-of-process), real provider credentials are already present in the child env and a live `claude -p` with a ~400K-token prompt would run and bill the operator's account without touching the cheval ledger the module guard watches.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the child environment from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG/LC_*, TMPDIR, CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN, FAKE_LOG, FAKE_LIMIT_TOKENS) instead of copying os.environ with a deny-list, so no credential can leak into the subprocess regardless of the developer's shell.
